summary.text: A large caravan tent housing a small-sized rock gambling den that arrives with the Jia merchant caravan at Gu Yue Village on Qing Mao Mountain.

claims.text: A grey-coloured tent of about one mu, counted as a large-sized tent, with two pillars at the entrance carved with an antithetical couplet. Inside, three rows of counters hold amber and fossil rocks of many sizes; person-tall rocks sit on the ground because they cannot fit on the counters, and Gu Masters inspect them in near silence.

Fang Yuan stops at a grey tent of about one mu, counted as a large-sized tent, with carved couplet pillars at the entrance among the caravan tents near Gu Yue Village. Inside, three rows of counters hold amber and fossil rocks of many sizes; person-tall rocks sit on the ground because they cannot fit on the counters, and Gu Masters inspect them in near silence. Counters sell at five, ten, or twenty primeval stones per rock, with rank one clerks on green belts serving buyers.

Rock gambling rests on Gu that self-seal into rock when starving. Outside, the rocks look alike; only opening them shows whether a live Gu, a dead Gu, or a solid core sits inside. This den is only small-sized: nine out of ten rocks are empty cores, and even filled rocks often hold dead Gu. Around Qing Mao Mountain such dens stay modest; farther east rock gambling dens grow larger, with named villages holding mega dens of long history.
Fang Yuan buys six purple gold fossils from the ten-stone counter for sixty primeval stones, refuses the free opening service, and grinds the rocks himself with Moonlight Gu light.
After a purple gold fossil is ground down to a rough yellow mudball,

Jia Jin Sheng, second young master on the caravan side and shopkeeper of this den, barges in when that mudball is palm-sized and offers forty primeval stones to buy it. Other Gu Masters name him as opening the den and treat a forced buy as breaking the den’s rules on Qing Mao Mountain Gu Yue ground. Fang Yuan refuses, finishes the open, and obtains a live Mudskin Toad, a rare rank two Gu priced at five hundred primeval stones, which Jia Jin Sheng then buys at that price after his usual surveillance methods fail to stop the win in front of the crowd. Fang Yuan leaves with five hundred and thirty-eight primeval stones and the last fossil still sealed.
